newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 5.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Wednesday's Daily Variety:
* General Electric's NBC is comfortably out front in Oscar sweeps, though down significantly from year-ago levels, and Walt Disney ABC is scrambling to reverse its own big year-to-year drop-offs.

* NBC and HBO topped the television nominations Tuesday for the Directors Guild of America Awards, boosted by multiple nods for "ER" and "The Larry Sanders Show." NBC earned eight nominations and HBO took six. ABC followed with three nominations.
* Direct expenditures on film and TV production in New York CIty rose 11 percent in 1996 to a record $2.2 billion, up from $2 billion the previous year.

* As Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer Inc moves to streamline operations and cautiously re-enter production, MGM Pictures president and chief operating officer Michael Marcus is understood to be ankling his position to pursue other interests.

* Producer-writer Warren Bell is expected to sign a three-year, $9 million overall development deal with Big Ticket Television, sources said. Bell's credits include Ellen, Coach and Uncle Buck and is expected to join Big Ticket Television later this year. He currently has an overall development deal at Walt Disney Television.
* President Clinton's State of the Union Address was forced to compete on Los Angeles television Tuesday night with the reading of the verdicts in the O.J. Simpson civil trial.
